summary.goal:
Build a small invoicing system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies) with a command-line interface, JSON persistence, tests and documentation. Follow every rule below exactly; the CLI output is machine-read.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/invoicing.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>`. Create the file (and its directory) on first use. Ids are integers per entity type, starting at 1.

Money: amounts are handled in integer cents internally and shown as decimal strings with exactly two decimals (`"12.30"`). Input amounts are decimal strings with at most two decimals; anything else (letters, three decimals, negative values) is an error. Rounding, wherever it is needed, is half up on the cent.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/money.js: parseMoney(text) -> cents, formatMoney(cents) -> string, roundCents(number) -> integer cents (half up).
- src/customers.js: addCustomer({ name, email }), a customer is { id, name, email }; email must contain "@".
- src/products.js: addProduct({ name, price, taxRate }), a product is { id, name, price (cents), taxRate (percent, integer 0-100, default 0) }.
- src/invoices.js:
  - createInvoice({ customerId, terms = 30 }) makes a draft: { id, number: null, customerId, status: "draft", terms, issued: null, due: null, lines: [], payments: [], subtotal: 0, tax: 0, total: 0, paid: 0, balance: 0 } (all amounts in cents).
  - addLine({ invoiceId, productId, quantity = 1, discount = 0 }) appends a line { productId, description (the product name), quantity (positive integer), unitPrice (cents), discount (percent, 0-100), net, tax } and recomputes the totals: net = unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100 rounded half up; tax = net * taxRate / 100 rounded half up; subtotal = sum of net; tax = sum of line tax; total = subtotal + tax; balance = total - paid. Only drafts accept lines.
  - issue({ invoiceId, today }) turns a draft with at least one line into status "issued": number becomes `INV-<year>-<nnnn>` with the year of `today` and a four-digit counter that starts at 0001 for each year and increments per issued invoice in that year; issued = today; due = today + terms days.
  - pay({ invoiceId, amount, today }) records { amount (cents), date } on an issued invoice; partial payments are allowed; paying more than the balance is an error; when paid reaches total the status becomes "paid".
  - voidInvoice({ invoiceId }) sets status "void" on a draft or on an issued invoice without payments; anything else is an error.
  - listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue, today } = {}); an invoice is overdue when its status is "issued" and due < today.
  - Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date.
- src/report.js:
  - aging({ today }) -> { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } summing the balance of issued invoices by how many days past due they are on `today` (not yet due -> current; 1-30 days past due -> days1to30; and so on; total is the sum of all five), in cents.
  - revenue() -> an array of { month: "YYYY-MM", invoices, total } for each month that has issued or paid invoices (by the issue date), sorted by month, totals in cents.

CLI: bin/invoice.js, run as `node bin/invoice.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints exactly one JSON value on stdout and exits 0; money fields in that JSON (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, amount, every aging bucket and revenue total) are formatted strings like "12.30", never raw cents. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2; an unknown command or a missing required option prints usage on stderr and exits 1.
- `add-customer --name <n> --email <e>` prints the customer.
- `add-product --name <n> --price <amount> [--tax <percent>]` prints the product.
- `create --customer <id> [--terms <days>]` prints the draft invoice.
- `add-line --invoice <id> --product <id> [--quantity <n>] [--discount <percent>]` prints the invoice.
- `issue --invoice <id> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `pay --invoice <id> --amount <amount> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `void --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `show --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `list [--status <s>] [--customer <id>] [--overdue] [--today <date>]` prints an array of invoices.
- `report aging [--today <date>]` and `report revenue` print the report objects.
- `export --invoice <id>` prints (as a JSON string) the CSV text of the invoice lines with the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax` followed by one row per line, money as formatted strings, rows separated by "\n", no trailing newline.

Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs every test, and write a README.md that documents the modules, every command with an example, and the rules. npm test must pass.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/invoicing.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>`. Create the file (and its directory) on first use. Ids are integers per entity type, starting at 1.

Money: amounts are handled in integer cents internally and shown as decimal strings with exactly two decimals (`"12.30"`). Input amounts are decimal strings with at most two decimals; anything else (letters, three decimals, negative values) is an error. Rounding, wherever it is needed, is half up on the cent.

- src/money.js: parseMoney(text) -> cents, formatMoney(cents) -> string, roundCents(number) -> integer cents (half up).
- src/customers.js: addCustomer({ name, email }), a customer is { id, name, email }; email must contain "@".
- src/products.js: addProduct({ name, price, taxRate }), a product is { id, name, price (cents), taxRate (percent, integer 0-100, default 0) }.
- src/invoices.js:
  - createInvoice({ customerId, terms = 30 }) makes a draft: { id, number: null, customerId, status: "draft", terms, issued: null, due: null, lines: [], payments: [], subtotal: 0, tax: 0, total: 0, paid: 0, balance: 0 } (all amounts in cents).
  - addLine({ invoiceId, productId, quantity = 1, discount = 0 }) appends a line { productId, description (the product name), quantity (positive integer), unitPrice (cents), discount (percent, 0-100), net, tax } and recomputes the totals: net = unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100 rounded half up; tax = net * taxRate / 100 rounded half up; subtotal = sum of net; tax = sum of line tax; total = subtotal + tax; balance = total - paid. Only drafts accept lines.
  - issue({ invoiceId, today }) turns a draft with at least one line into status "issued": number becomes `INV-<year>-<nnnn>` with the year of `today` and a four-digit counter that starts at 0001 for each year and increments per issued invoice in that year; issued = today; due = today + terms days.
  - pay({ invoiceId, amount, today }) records { amount (cents), date } on an issued invoice; partial payments are allowed; paying more than the balance is an error; when paid reaches total the status becomes "paid".
  - voidInvoice({ invoiceId }) sets status "void" on a draft or on an issued invoice without payments; anything else is an error.
  - listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue, today } = {}); an invoice is overdue when its status is "issued" and due < today.

- `add-product --name <n> --price <amount> [--tax <percent>]` prints the product.
- `create --customer <id> [--terms <days>]` prints the draft invoice.
- `add-line --invoice <id> --product <id> [--quantity <n>] [--discount <percent>]` prints the invoice.
- `issue --invoice <id> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.

- `void --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `show --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `list [--status <s>] [--customer <id>] [--overdue] [--today <date>]` prints an array of invoices.

tasks.spec:
Implement src/customers.js per design §4.4: `addCustomer({ name, email }, store = getStore())` allocates the next customer id with `nextId`, appends `{ id, name, email }` to `store.customers` and returns the stored object. `name` must contain at least one non-space character, else throw `Error("name is required")`; `email` must be a non-empty string containing `"@"`, else throw `Error('invalid email: "<email>"')` (`email is required` when missing or empty). Import the store helpers from ./store.js; do not format money here.

Tests in test/customers.test.js (node:test + node:assert/strict) with an explicit store from `createStore()`: two customers get ids 1 and 2, the returned object is the one stored, a second store allocates ids independently, and every rejection case (missing name, blank name, email without `@`, empty email) throws with the documented message. Do not touch the filesystem.

acceptance.review: Confirm the module only reads and writes the store passed in (no hidden globals besides the getStore() default).

report.summary:
Implemented src/customers.js per design §4.4 and added test/customers.test.js.

`addCustomer({ name, email }, store = getStore())` validates first, then allocates the id with `nextId(store, "customer")`, appends `{ id, name, email }` to `store.customers` and returns that exact stored object. Validation: `name` must be a string with at least one non-space character else `Error("name is required")`; a missing, non-string, empty or whitespace-only `email` gives `Error("email is required")`, and any other string without `"@"` gives `Error('invalid email: "<email>"')`. The module imports only `getStore` and `nextId` from ./store.js, touches nothing but the store passed in, does no formatting and does no I/O.

The id is allocated after validation, so a rejected call leaves both the customers array and the counter untouched — this is why the module validates into locals rather than inline in the pushed object literal.

Test file uses node:test + node:assert/strict with explicit `createStore()` stores only (no filesystem): ids 1 and 2 in order, the returned object is identical (`assert.equal`) to `store.customers[0]`, two separate stores allocate ids independently, allocation continues from a pre-set counter, and all four rejection cases (missing/non-string name, blank name, missing/empty/whitespace/non-string email, email without `@`) assert the documented messages plus that nothing was stored.
report.evidence: `node --test test/customers.test.js` -> 9 tests, 9 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. `npm test` (node --test, whole suite including the foundation tests) -> 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail, exit 0.
decisions: The destructured first parameter defaults to `{}` (`addCustomer({ name, email } = {}, store = getStore())`), so calling it with no arguments still produces the documented `name is required` error instead of a TypeError. All documented call shapes are unaffected.
Validation happens before `nextId`, so a failed add does not consume a customer id; a test pins this behaviour.
A whitespace-only email is treated as missing (`email is required`) rather than as an invalid address, since it is empty for practical purposes.
`name` and `email` are stored exactly as given, without trimming, matching the design's plain `{ id, name, email }` shape.

tasks.spec:

acceptance.review: Confirm price is stored in cents and that the module never formats money.

report.summary:
Implemented `src/products.js` per design §4.5 and its unit tests in `test/products.test.js`.

`addProduct({ name, price, taxRate = 0 } = {}, store = getStore())` validates the name (string with at least one non-space character, else `name is required`), parses the price with `parseMoney` (so `price` is stored in integer cents and non-strings/three-decimal/negative values fail there with `invalid amount: "<x>"`), validates `taxRate` as an integer 0-100 (else `invalid tax rate: <v>`), then allocates the id through `nextId(store, "product")`, appends `{ id, name, price, taxRate }` and returns the stored product. Validation happens before the id is allocated, so rejected calls leave the store and its counter untouched. The module never formats money: it imports only `parseMoney` and `{ getStore, nextId }`, so no serialize/csv/formatMoney code is reachable.

Tests use an explicit `createStore()` and never touch the filesystem: ids 1 and 2 with the products appended to `store.products`, cents conversion for `"12"`, `"12.3"`, `"12.30"`, `"0.01"`, `"0"`, `"1999.99"`, `taxRate` defaulting to 0 and the 0/100 bounds, frozen key order `id, name, price, taxRate`, a missing price, the seven bad price forms (`"1.234"`, `"abc"`, the number `1230`, `""`, `"-1.00"`, `"1,00"`, leading/trailing space), six bad tax rates (`101`, `-1`, `8.5`, `"8"`, `null`, `NaN`), five bad names (`undefined`, `""`, `"   "`, `42`, `null`) and the guarantee that a rejected call does not consume an id.

Both acceptance commands exit 0: `node --test test/products.test.js` is 9/9 pass; `npm test` is 55/55 pass (my 9 plus the foundation's 46).
report.evidence: `node --test test/products.test.js` -> tests 9, pass 9, fail 0, exit 0. `npm test` -> tests 55, pass 55, fail 0, exit 0. `git status --short` shows only the expected modified/untracked entries and no new files outside my scope; grep confirms src/products.js imports nothing from serialize/csv and never calls formatMoney.
decisions: Validation order is name, then price (via parseMoney), then taxRate; when a call is bad in more than one way the name error wins, then the amount error. The design fixes the messages but not the order.
The id is allocated only after all validation passes, so a rejected addProduct does not burn a product id (added a test for it).
A name of non-string type (e.g. 42, null, undefined) throws `name is required`, matching the design's 'at least one non-space character' rule rather than a type error.
`taxRate` accepts exactly integers in 0-100: floats like 8.5, numeric strings like "8", null and NaN are all rejected with `invalid tax rate: <v>`.

tasks.title: Invoices module: drafts, lines, issue, pay, void, list
tasks.spec:
Implement src/invoices.js per design §4.6 and the rounding/numbering rules of §5. Export `createInvoice`, `addLine`, `issue`, `pay`, `voidInvoice`, `listInvoices`, each taking `store = getStore()` as an optional second argument, each mutating the store and returning the stored invoice (or the filtered array). Use `parseMoney`, `roundCents` from ./money.js and `todayISO`, `addDays`, `isValidDate` from ./dates.js; never format money.

Key boundaries: the draft shape and key order are frozen (design §3); `addLine` snapshots the product name, price and tax rate into the line and recomputes `subtotal`, `tax`, `total` and `balance`; `issue` derives the number as the highest existing `INV-<year>-nnnn` suffix for the year plus one, padded to four digits, and sets `issued`/`due` from `today` and `terms`; `pay` only applies to issued invoices and rejects amounts above the balance; `voidInvoice` accepts drafts and unpaid issued invoices only; `listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue, today } = {})` applies the given filters conjunctively in store order. Error messages come from the catalogue in design §5. Do not check that the customer of a new invoice exists (design §8.2).

Tests in test/invoices.test.js, using explicit stores built with `createStore()` plus `addCustomer`/`addProduct`: the empty draft shape; line net/tax rounding at a `.5` cent boundary; totals recomputed after a second line; rejection of lines on non-draft invoices, unknown invoice/product, bad quantity and bad discount; issuing without lines; numbering `INV-2026-0001`, `INV-2026-0002`, and a fresh per-year counter for another year, including a reload of the store from disk before the second issue; `due` = today + terms across a month boundary; partial payment leaving `issued`, full payment flipping to `paid` with `balance` 0, and overpayment rejected; void rules (draft ok, unpaid issued ok, paid or partially paid issued rejected, already void rejected); and list filters including `--overdue` semantics (`due < today`, so due today is not overdue).

report.summary: Implemented src/invoices.js per design §4.6 (createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices, each with an optional `store = getStore()` second argument) and test/invoices.test.js (18 tests). tasks.title: Reports: aging and revenue
tasks.spec:
Implement src/report.js per design §4.7: `aging({ today = todayISO() } = {}, store = getStore())` and `revenue(store = getStore())`, both returning integer cents and no formatted strings. Aging counts only `status === "issued"` invoices, buckets them by `daysBetween(due, today)` (`<= 0` current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, `> 90` over90) summing `balance`, with `total` the sum of the five buckets. Revenue groups `"issued"` and `"paid"` invoices by `monthOf(issued)`, sorted ascending by month, each row `{ month, invoices, total }` with `total` the sum of invoice `total`.

Tests in test/report.test.js build fixtures through `createStore()` + `addCustomer`/`addProduct`/`createInvoice`/`addLine`/`issue`/`pay` with explicit `today` values: every bucket including a boundary case for exactly 1, 30, 31, 90 and 91 days past due, due today landing in `current`, paid and void and draft invoices excluded, `total` equal to the bucket sum, an empty store giving all zeros, and revenue across two months sorted ascending with paid invoices still counted.

acceptance.review: Confirm boundary days land in the documented buckets and that nothing is formatted as a string.

report.summary: Implemented src/report.js per design §4.7 and its tests. `aging({ today = todayISO() } = {}, store = getStore())` counts only invoices with status "issued", buckets each by `daysBetween(due, today)` (<=0 current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, >90) summing `balance`, and sets `total` to the sum of the five buckets; keys are emitted in the frozen order current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total. `revenue(store = getStore())` groups "issued" and "paid" invoices by `monthOf(issued)` into `{ month, invoices, total }` rows, skips invoices with no issue date, and sorts ascending by month via a Map (month order, not store order). Both return integer cents only; the module imports no formatting code. test/report.test.js has 11 tests built through createStore/addCustomer/addProduct/createInvoice/addLine/issue/pay/voidInvoice with explicit today values: empty store all zeros; a nine-invoice store with issue dates set so invoices are exactly 0, 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91 and 200 days past due plus one not yet due (buckets 2000 each, total 10000, total re-checked as the bucket sum); a dedicated boundary test stepping one invoice's due through 0/1/30/31/60/61/90/91 days and asserting the exact bucket each time (due today -> current); draft/paid/void exclusion; a partial payment leaving 600 cents in over90; integer-cents plus key-order checks; invalid today; and revenue tests for two months created in reverse order still ascending, paid counted with draft/void skipped, same-month accumulation, and an empty array for an empty store.
report.evidence: `node --test test/report.test.js` -> tests 11, pass 11, fail 0, exit 0. `npm test` -> tests 84, pass 84, fail 0, exit 0 (full suite including the parallel executors' modules).
decisions: aging validates `today` explicitly with isValidDate before scanning invoices, throwing `invalid date: "<v>"`, so a bad date fails even when the store has no issued invoices (the design left this implicit; the CLI needs `report aging --today 2026-02-30` to exit 2, and the message matches the shared catalogue).

Revenue rows are accumulated in a Map keyed by month and sorted with a string comparison on "YYYY-MM", so ordering is by month rather than by store/insertion order; the test creates a February invoice before a January one to pin this.

Only `status === "issued"` counts for aging and only `"issued"`/`"paid"` for revenue; void, draft and paid are excluded from aging, and the buckets are summed into `total` after the scan (which also fixes the key order).

tasks.title: Output serialization and CSV export
tasks.spec:
Implement the output boundary per design §4.8 and §4.9. src/serialize.js exports `publicCustomer`, `publicProduct`, `publicInvoice`, `publicAging`, `publicRevenue`, each returning a new object with the exact key order of design §3/§4.8 and every money field (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, payment amount, all six aging fields, revenue total) converted with `formatMoney`; inputs must not be mutated. src/csv.js exports `invoiceCsv(invoice)` producing the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax`, one row per line, rows joined with `\n` and no trailing newline, money formatted, quantity and discount plain integers, and fields quoted only when they contain `,`, `"` or a newline.

Tests in test/serialize.test.js and test/csv.test.js: every entity round-shaped from a real store fixture, key order asserted with `Object.keys`, no cents leaking as numbers, the source objects unchanged after serialization, aging and revenue rows formatted, and CSV output for a multi-line invoice plus an empty-line invoice (header only) and a description containing a comma.

acceptance.review: Confirm this is the only module converting cents to strings and that no money value reaches output as a number.

report.summary: Implemented the output boundary: src/serialize.js and src/csv.js, with test/serialize.test.js (11 tests) and test/csv.test.js (5 tests). src/serialize.js exports the five documented functions and nothing else — publicCustomer, publicProduct, publicInvoice, publicAging, publicRevenue — each returning a brand-new object with the design's frozen key order, converting every money field through formatMoney (product price; line unitPrice/net/tax; invoice subtotal/tax/total/paid/balance; payment amount; all six aging buckets including total; revenue total) while leaving quantities, discounts, taxRate, counts, dates and ids untouched. Line and payment views are module-private helpers mapped inside publicInvoice, so stored data can never be aliased or mutated by a caller. src/csv.js's invoiceCsv emits the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax` followed by one row per line, rows joined with "\n" and no trailing newline (header alone for an invoice with no lines); quantity and discount are bare integers, unitPrice/net/tax go through formatMoney, and a field is wrapped in double quotes with inner quotes doubled only when it contains a comma, a double quote or a newline. Both modules import only src/money.js, so they are the single place cents become strings; no other module formats money and no money value leaves as a number. Tests build real fixtures through createStore/addCustomer/addProduct/createInvoice/addLine/issue/pay plus aging/revenue, assert exact formatted values and Object.keys order at every level, verify the sources are unchanged (structuredClone comparison) and that views are new objects, and cover CSV for a multi-line invoice, a header-only invoice, a comma description, and embedded quotes/newlines.
report.evidence: From the project root: `npm test` -> 100 tests, 100 pass, 0 fail (includes my 16 and all previously existing suites). `node --test test/serialize.test.js` -> 11 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail. `node --test test/serialize.test.js test/csv.test.js` -> 16 pass, 0 fail. Pinned values in the tests: a real invoice with lines costing 1800+144 and 750 renders as subtotal "25.50", tax "1.44", total "26.94", paid "5.00", balance "21.94", unitPrice "10.00"/"2.50", net "18.00"/"7.50", tax "1.44"/"0.00", payment amount "5.00"; aging on that invoice 77 days past due is days61to90 "21.94", total "21.94", others "0.00"; revenue is [{ month: "2026-03", invoices: 1, total: "26.94" }]; CSV for the comma-named product is `"Widget, large",2,10.00,10,18.00,1.44` with the header-only output equal to the header string exactly. Tests use in-memory stores only, so no data/ directory was created (verified: repository still contains just package.json, src, test).
decisions: publicLine/publicPayment are module-private rather than exported: the design names only five exports and the CLI needs no more; their formatting is covered through publicInvoice.
publicRevenue returns a new array of new row objects and publicInvoice returns new arrays for lines/payments, so serialization never aliases or mutates stored data.
invoiceCsv quotes with the regex /[",\n]/ and uses String() on each column, so quantity/discount render as plain integers and a numeric field could never trip the quoting path.
The header row is always present, even for an invoice with zero lines, and no trailing newline is emitted (asserted directly).

tasks.title: CLI entry point: parsing, dispatch, exit codes
tasks.spec:
Implement src/cli.js and bin/invoice.js exactly per design §4.10 and §6. `main(argv)` returns `{ code, stdout, stderr }` strings and performs no I/O: it strips `--data <path>` (default `data/invoicing.json`), parses `--key value` options plus the `--overdue` flag, dispatches the twelve command forms of the table in §6, loads the store with `loadStore`, calls the domain function, saves with `saveStore` for the seven mutating commands, and returns compact `JSON.stringify(value) + "\n"` on stdout. Failures return `JSON.stringify({ error: message }) + "\n"` on stderr with code 2; unknown command, unknown option, missing option value, missing required option, wrong positionals, or a missing/unknown `report` subcommand return the usage block of §6 on stderr with code 1 and nothing on stdout. Id options are parsed strictly as positive integers (`invalid id: <token>`, code 2). `bin/invoice.js` only wires `main` to the process streams, sets the exit code, and carries the `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang.

Tests in test/cli.test.js: call `main` directly for the parsing surface (successful output shape per command, each exit-1 usage case, each exit-2 error case including unknown ids and invalid money, `--data` accepted before and after the command), and spawn `bin/invoice.js` with `spawnSync` for the process-level contract (exit codes, stdout/stderr separation, the JSON file and its directory created on first use, state persisted between runs). Use temp directories via os.tmpdir() for data files.

acceptance.review: Confirm no console output or process.exit inside src/cli.js, that stdout carries exactly one JSON value plus one newline, and that usage errors never print JSON.

report.summary:
Implemented the CLI layer: src/cli.js exports `main(argv) -> { code, stdout, stderr }` as pure string-returning code (no console, no process, no I/O of its own beyond the store module), and bin/invoice.js is the shebang wrapper that writes the two strings to the two streams and exits with the returned code.

Parsing: `--data <path>` is stripped anywhere in argv (default `data/invoicing.json`, a working-directory-relative path), `--overdue` is the only value-less flag, all other options are `--key value` pairs. Options are validated per command, so an unknown option, an option the command does not accept, a missing option value, a missing required option, a wrong positional count, an unknown command, or a missing/unknown `report` subcommand all produce the §6 usage block on stderr with exit 1, before the store is loaded (so no data file appears for a usage error). All twelve command forms dispatch through loadStore, the domain function, and — for the seven mutating commands (add-customer, add-product, create, add-line, issue, pay, void) — saveStore. Success prints one compact `JSON.stringify(value) + "\n"` on stdout with empty stderr and exit 0; every thrown error (bad id, bad money/date/rate, missing entity, corrupt data file) prints `{"error":"<message>"}` on stderr with empty stdout and exit 2. Id options are parsed with /^[1-9]\d*$/ and throw `invalid id: <token>`; quantity/discount/tax/terms are converted to numbers only when they look like integers, otherwise the raw token is passed to the domain function so the catalogue message echoes it verbatim.

Tests: test/cli.test.js has 25 tests — direct `main` calls for the parsing surface (per-command success shape and key order, the twelve-command newline/JSON contract, `--data` before and after the command, 22 usage cases, 16 value-error cases, the stateful domain errors plus a check that a failed mutation leaves the file unchanged, corrupt JSON), and spawnSync tests of the real binary (full workflow persisting across runs, exit-code and stdout/stderr separation, default `data/invoicing.json` created under the cwd). All data files are under os.tmpdir(), so no test touches the repository's data/.
report.evidence: `npm test` -> tests 125, pass 125, fail 0, exit 0 (my 25 plus the 100 from earlier tasks). `node --test test/cli.test.js` -> tests 25, pass 25, fail 0, exit 0. Manual end-to-end run of add-customer / add-product / create / add-line / issue / pay / list / report aging / report revenue / export against a temp data file printed correctly formatted JSON and exited 0; a manual sweep of no-command, unknown command, `report`/`report bogus`, extra positional, missing required option, unknown option, missing option value, `show --invoice abc` and `--price 1.234` produced exit 1 with usage on stderr and exit 2 with the JSON error object respectively, with empty stdout in every case. Grep for `console\.|process\.|require\(` in src/cli.js returned no matches. Verified no `data/` directory was created in the repository by the test run.
decisions: Options are whitelisted per command: an option that the dispatched command does not accept (e.g. `show --today`, `report revenue --today`) is an exit-1 usage error, same as an unknown option. The design gives a per-command option column but does not say whether a known-but-inapplicable option counts as unknown; treating it as unknown avoids silently ignoring typos. `--data` is accepted by every command.

The default data path is kept as the literal relative string "data/invoicing.json" rather than path.resolve()d, so it resolves against the cwd as required while error messages stay readable and relative.

quantity/discount/taxRate/terms tokens are converted to numbers only when they match /^-?\d+$/; otherwise the raw string goes to the domain function so its message echoes the raw token (e.g. `invalid quantity: x`, `invalid tax rate: eight`). Id options use the stricter /^[1-9]\d*$/ with `invalid id: <token>`.

Parse/validation of the command line happens entirely before loadStore, so a usage error never creates the data file; only a valid command triggers file creation (including read-only commands, per §6).

`list --today <bogus>` is not rejected by the CLI: listInvoices compares date strings without validating, and the design says bad dates fail via the domain functions. `issue`, `pay` and `report aging` do validate and exit 2.
openIssues: package.json has no "bin" entry; the design's package.json spec mentions only type/scripts and package.json is outside this task's file scope, so the CLI is invoked as `node bin/invoice.js` (which is what §6 documents).

tasks.spec:
Add test/cli.e2e.test.js that drives the real binary the way a user would, with `spawnSync(process.execPath, ["bin/invoice.js", ...], { cwd: repoRoot, encoding: "utf8" })` and `--data <tempdir>/invoicing.json`. Cover the full workflow in order: add two customers (ids 1 and 2), add two products with different tax rates, create a draft with `--terms` and check the zero-amount draft output, add two lines with quantity and discount and check the recomputed formatted totals, issue it with an explicit `--today` and check the number, `issued` and `due`, pay a part and then the rest and check status/paid/balance, show the invoice, list with `--status`, `--customer` and `--overdue`, `report aging` with a past `--today` that lands in a bucket, `report revenue` for the issue month, and `export` whose stdout JSON-parses to the CSV text of the lines. Also assert: unknown command and a missing required option exit 1 with usage text on stderr and empty stdout; an overpayment exits 2 with `{ error }` on stderr and empty stdout; the data file is created on first use; a second process run sees the earlier state and continues the ids.

This test may surface real defects. Fix them in the owning module with the smallest correct change and mention each fix in your report; keep the whole suite green. Prefer changing only the test file.

acceptance.review: Confirm the workflow asserts real observable behaviour end to end, that any fix outside the test file is minimal and explained, and that the suite is green.

It also asserts exit 1 + the exact usage block on stderr with empty stdout for an unknown command, no command, an unknown report subcommand and missing required options; exit 2 with `{"error":"payment exceeds balance: 99.00"}` on stderr and empty stdout for an overpayment (plus that the invoice is unchanged afterwards); that the data file and its parent directory are created on first use (by a mutation and, separately, by a read-only `list`); and that a second process run sees the earlier state and continues the ids. decisions: The workflow needs an unpaid, overdue invoice for `list --overdue` and `report aging` to be meaningful, since the required 'pay a part then the rest' step settles the first invoice into status paid (which aging excludes). projectEvents.summary: Built the shared foundation: test runner wiring, money, dates and JSON store modules, with full node:test coverage. package.json gained only the test script (no dependencies); .gitignore gained data/; src/money.js implements parseMoney/formatMoney/roundCents exactly per design §4.1 (strict regex, string-splitting, two-decimal output, Math.round half-up); src/dates.js implements todayISO/isValidDate/addDays/daysBetween/monthOf UTC-based per §4.2; src/store.js implements createStore/loadStore/saveStore/nextId/getById/getStore/setStore per §4.3 including creating the file and parent directory on first use and the corrupt-JSON error. Three test files cover accepted/rejected money inputs, half-up boundaries, zero-padded formatting, impossible calendar dates, month/year/leap-day crossings, store creation, round trip, counter continuation and clamping, and corrupt JSON; all file tests use os.tmpdir() via fs.mkdtempSync.

Implemented src/customers.js per design §4.4 and added test/customers.test.js.

`addCustomer({ name, email }, store = getStore())` validates first, then allocates the id with `nextId(store, "customer")`, appends `{ id, name, email }` to `store.customers` and returns that exact stored object. Validation: `name` must be a string with at least one non-space character else `Error("name is required")`; a missing, non-string, empty or whitespace-only `email` gives `Error("email is required")`, and any other string without `"@"` gives `Error('invalid email: "<email>"')`. The module imports only `getStore` and `nextId` from ./store.js, touches nothing but the store passed in, does no formatting and does no I/O.

The id is allocated after validation, so a rejected call leaves both the customers array and the counter untouched — this is why the module validates into locals rather than inline in the pushed object literal.

Test file uses node:test + node:assert/strict with explicit `createStore()` stores only (no filesystem): ids 1 and 2 in order, the returned object is identical (`assert.equal`) to `store.customers[0]`, two separate stores allocate ids independently, allocation continues from a pre-set counter, and all four rejection cases (missing/non-string name, blank name, missing/empty/whitespace/non-string email, email without `@`) assert the documented messages plus that nothing was stored.

Implemented `src/products.js` per design §4.5 and its unit tests in `test/products.test.js`.

`addProduct({ name, price, taxRate = 0 } = {}, store = getStore())` validates the name (string with at least one non-space character, else `name is required`), parses the price with `parseMoney` (so `price` is stored in integer cents and non-strings/three-decimal/negative values fail there with `invalid amount: "<x>"`), validates `taxRate` as an integer 0-100 (else `invalid tax rate: <v>`), then allocates the id through `nextId(store, "product")`, appends `{ id, name, price, taxRate }` and returns the stored product. Validation happens before the id is allocated, so rejected calls leave the store and its counter untouched. The module never formats money: it imports only `parseMoney` and `{ getStore, nextId }`, so no serialize/csv/formatMoney code is reachable.

Tests use an explicit `createStore()` and never touch the filesystem: ids 1 and 2 with the products appended to `store.products`, cents conversion for `"12"`, `"12.3"`, `"12.30"`, `"0.01"`, `"0"`, `"1999.99"`, `taxRate` defaulting to 0 and the 0/100 bounds, frozen key order `id, name, price, taxRate`, a missing price, the seven bad price forms (`"1.234"`, `"abc"`, the number `1230`, `""`, `"-1.00"`, `"1,00"`, leading/trailing space), six bad tax rates (`101`, `-1`, `8.5`, `"8"`, `null`, `NaN`), five bad names (`undefined`, `""`, `"   "`, `42`, `null`) and the guarantee that a rejected call does not consume an id.

Both acceptance commands exit 0: `node --test test/products.test.js` is 9/9 pass; `npm test` is 55/55 pass (my 9 plus the foundation's 46).

projectEvents.summary: Implemented src/invoices.js per design §4.6 (createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices, each with an optional `store = getStore()` second argument) and test/invoices.test.js (18 tests). Drafts use the frozen key order of §3 and are created without checking that the customer exists (§8.2); addLine only works on drafts, snapshots the product's name/price/taxRate into the line and recomputes subtotal/tax/total/balance; issue derives INV-<year>-<nnnn> from the highest existing suffix for that year in the store, sets issued/due from today and terms; pay applies only to issued invoices, allows zero and partial payments, rejects amounts above the balance and flips to paid at settlement; voidInvoice accepts drafts and unpaid issued invoices; listInvoices filters by status, customerId and overdue (due < today) conjunctively in store order. The module imports only parseMoney/roundCents, todayISO/addDays/isValidDate and store helpers, so no money formatting happens here and amounts stay integer cents.

Implemented src/report.js per design §4.7 and its tests. `aging({ today = todayISO() } = {}, store = getStore())` counts only invoices with status "issued", buckets each by `daysBetween(due, today)` (<=0 current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, >90) summing `balance`, and sets `total` to the sum of the five buckets; keys are emitted in the frozen order current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total. `revenue(store = getStore())` groups "issued" and "paid" invoices by `monthOf(issued)` into `{ month, invoices, total }` rows, skips invoices with no issue date, and sorts ascending by month via a Map (month order, not store order). Both return integer cents only; the module imports no formatting code. test/report.test.js has 11 tests built through createStore/addCustomer/addProduct/createInvoice/addLine/issue/pay/voidInvoice with explicit today values: empty store all zeros; a nine-invoice store with issue dates set so invoices are exactly 0, 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91 and 200 days past due plus one not yet due (buckets 2000 each, total 10000, total re-checked as the bucket sum); a dedicated boundary test stepping one invoice's due through 0/1/30/31/60/61/90/91 days and asserting the exact bucket each time (due today -> current); draft/paid/void exclusion; a partial payment leaving 600 cents in over90; integer-cents plus key-order checks; invalid today; and revenue tests for two months created in reverse order still ascending, paid counted with draft/void skipped, same-month accumulation, and an empty array for an empty store.

projectEvents.summary: Implemented the output boundary: src/serialize.js and src/csv.js, with test/serialize.test.js (11 tests) and test/csv.test.js (5 tests). src/serialize.js exports the five documented functions and nothing else — publicCustomer, publicProduct, publicInvoice, publicAging, publicRevenue — each returning a brand-new object with the design's frozen key order, converting every money field through formatMoney (product price; line unitPrice/net/tax; invoice subtotal/tax/total/paid/balance; payment amount; all six aging buckets including total; revenue total) while leaving quantities, discounts, taxRate, counts, dates and ids untouched. Line and payment views are module-private helpers mapped inside publicInvoice, so stored data can never be aliased or mutated by a caller. src/csv.js's invoiceCsv emits the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax` followed by one row per line, rows joined with "\n" and no trailing newline (header alone for an invoice with no lines); quantity and discount are bare integers, unitPrice/net/tax go through formatMoney, and a field is wrapped in double quotes with inner quotes doubled only when it contains a comma, a double quote or a newline. Both modules import only src/money.js, so they are the single place cents become strings; no other module formats money and no money value leaves as a number. Tests build real fixtures through createStore/addCustomer/addProduct/createInvoice/addLine/issue/pay plus aging/revenue, assert exact formatted values and Object.keys order at every level, verify the sources are unchanged (structuredClone comparison) and that views are new objects, and cover CSV for a multi-line invoice, a header-only invoice, a comma description, and embedded quotes/newlines.

projectEvents.note: cli · src/cli.js validates options per command: `--overdue` is the only flag, every other option takes a value, and an option that the dispatched command does not accept (e.g. `show --today`, `report revenue --today`) is an exit-1 usage error just like an unknown option. The design lists a per-command option column and says unknown options are usage errors, but does not state whether a globally-known-but-inapplicable option counts; treating it as unknown keeps typos (and stray options) from being silently ignored. Tests pin this. `--data` is allowed for every command and is parsed before the command is resolved, so it can appear anywhere.

cli · The `--data` default is the literal relative string "data/invoicing.json", not path.resolve()d: it resolves against the process working directory the same way (store.js reads/writes it directly), and keeping it relative means `data file is not valid JSON: data/invoicing.json` stays readable in output. Option values for quantity/discount/tax/terms are converted to numbers only when they match /^-?\d+$/; anything else is handed to the domain function unchanged so the catalogue message echoes the raw token (e.g. `invalid quantity: x`). Id options (`--customer`, `--invoice`, `--product`) are parsed with /^[1-9]\d*$/ and throw `invalid id: <token>` (exit 2) otherwise. list/report use today is not validated by the CLI beyond what the domain functions do (listInvoices compares ISO strings without validating), matching the design's "bad money/dates/rates come from the domain functions".

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented the CLI layer: src/cli.js exports `main(argv) -> { code, stdout, stderr }` as pure string-returning code (no console, no process, no I/O of its own beyond the store module), and bin/invoice.js is the shebang wrapper that writes the two strings to the two streams and exits with the returned code.

Parsing: `--data <path>` is stripped anywhere in argv (default `data/invoicing.json`, a working-directory-relative path), `--overdue` is the only value-less flag, all other options are `--key value` pairs. Options are validated per command, so an unknown option, an option the command does not accept, a missing option value, a missing required option, a wrong positional count, an unknown command, or a missing/unknown `report` subcommand all produce the §6 usage block on stderr with exit 1, before the store is loaded (so no data file appears for a usage error). All twelve command forms dispatch through loadStore, the domain function, and — for the seven mutating commands (add-customer, add-product, create, add-line, issue, pay, void) — saveStore. Success prints one compact `JSON.stringify(value) + "\n"` on stdout with empty stderr and exit 0; every thrown error (bad id, bad money/date/rate, missing entity, corrupt data file) prints `{"error":"<message>"}` on stderr with empty stdout and exit 2. Id options are parsed with /^[1-9]\d*$/ and throw `invalid id: <token>`; quantity/discount/tax/terms are converted to numbers only when they look like integers, otherwise the raw token is passed to the domain function so the catalogue message echoes it verbatim.

Tests: test/cli.test.js has 25 tests — direct `main` calls for the parsing surface (per-command success shape and key order, the twelve-command newline/JSON contract, `--data` before and after the command, 22 usage cases, 16 value-error cases, the stateful domain errors plus a check that a failed mutation leaves the file unchanged, corrupt JSON), and spawnSync tests of the real binary (full workflow persisting across runs, exit-code and stdout/stderr separation, default `data/invoicing.json` created under the cwd). All data files are under os.tmpdir(), so no test touches the repository's data/.

projectEvents.summary: Added test/cli.e2e.test.js, an end-to-end test that spawns the real binary (`spawnSync(process.execPath, ["bin/invoice.js", ...], { cwd: REPO_ROOT, encoding: "utf8" })`) against a fresh temp data path (`<mkdtemp>/nested/invoicing.json`, a directory that does not exist yet) and drives the whole CLI contract in order: add two customers and two products with different tax rates (ids continue to 2 across separate processes), create a draft with `--terms` and assert the exact zero-amount draft JSON, add two lines with quantity and discount and assert the recomputed formatted totals (including a half-up tax rounding case: 47.50 * 5% = 2.375 -> "2.38"), issue with `--today` and assert number/issued/due, pay a part then the rest and assert status/paid/balance/payments, show the invoice in a new process, add a second unpaid invoice so list/aging/revenue have something to report, list by `--status`, `--customer` and `--overdue`, `report aging --today 2026-04-01` landing in days1to30, `report revenue` for both issue months, and `export` whose stdout JSON-parses to the exact CSV (header, formatted money, no trailing newline). It also asserts exit 1 + the exact usage block on stderr with empty stdout for an unknown command, no command, an unknown report subcommand and missing required options; exit 2 with `{"error":"payment exceeds balance: 99.00"}` on stderr and empty stdout for an overpayment (plus that the invoice is unchanged afterwards); that the data file and its parent directory are created on first use (by a mutation and, separately, by a read-only `list`); and that a second process run sees the earlier state and continues the ids. No defects surfaced, so no source file needed changing — the only new file is the test.

Wrote README.md (693 lines) documenting the invoicing system: intro, requirements (Node >= 18, `node --test`, zero dependencies, no build step), layout, `npm test`, storage (default `data/invoicing.json` created on first use, `--data <path>` on every command, `data/` gitignored, on-disk JSON shape, counters), the money rules (integer cents inside, two-decimal strings out with an accepted-input table for `parseMoney`/`formatMoney`/`roundCents`), a module reference for every `src/` module with its exported signatures, a CLI section covering all twelve command forms from design §6 (each with a copy-pasteable example and output), the exit-code/stderr contract with a table of twenty real error messages, and a business-rules section covering numbering, terms/due dates, line maths, partial payments, voiding, overdue, aging buckets and revenue.

Every example was run against a scratch `--data` path and the real output is pasted.
